intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF5B gene (602809) on chromosome 10p11.22.

paragraphs.text: Kyphomelic dysplasia is a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias with severe limb bowing and variable findings such as narrow thorax and abnormal facies (Itai et al., 2022). The form caused by heterozygous KIF5B mutation is marked by sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Itai et al. (2022) noted that it extends the phenotypic spectrum of kinesinopathies.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) reported 4 individuals from 4 families with kyphomelic dysplasia. All of them had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Three individuals had short stature. Three developed postnatal osteoporosis followed by fractures, 2 had brachycephaly, and 2 were diagnosed with optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to study 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. All 4 carried de novo heterozygous mutations in the KIF5B gene, which encodes kinesin-1 heavy chain. Two had a c.272A-G transition resulting in a lys91-to-arg (K91R) substitution, 1 had a c.584C-A transversion resulting in a thr195-to-lys (T195K) substitution, and 1 had a c.701G-T transversion resulting in a gly234-to-val (G234V) substitution. Each mutation affected a conserved amino acid in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of KIF5B.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) described 3 additional patients with heterozygous KIF5B variants, none of whom had skeletal dysplasia. The first was a 9-year-old boy with a de novo leu537-to-pro (L537P) variant. He had severe developmental delay and intellectual disability, early-onset refractory epilepsy, hypotonia, feeding difficulties requiring gastrostomy, progressive cortical atrophy, a thin corpus callosum, and severe scoliosis. His perinatal period was complicated by respiratory distress requiring ventilation.

paragraphs.text: The second patient described by Flex et al. (2023) was a 67-year-old man from a family segregating an autosomal dominant, paternally inherited in-frame deletion (asn255del). Affected members of this family (the father and 3 sibs) developed dilated cardiomyopathy in their sixth decade, and 3 of them required heart transplant. The cardiomyopathy was associated with a skeletal myopathy that worsened over time, ophthalmoplegia, elevated creatine phosphokinase, joint contractures, and peripheral neuropathy. Clubfoot was also reported.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) reviewed their patients together with the 4 previously reported patients with KIF5B-related kyphomelic dysplasia. The authors proposed grouping these phenotypes, which share hypotonia, developmental delay/intellectual disability, and a suggestive facial gestalt, as KIF5B-related diseases.

paragraphs.text: Flex et al. (2023) injected zebrafish embryos with mRNA encoding the kyphomelic dysplasia-associated KIF5B T195K variant. At 2 days postfertilization (dpf), the embryos had defects in heart size and morphology with cardiac edema. At 3 dpf, the ceratohyal cartilage angle was wider. Mitochondrial coverage along motoneuron axons was reduced. These findings were consistent with a dominant, possibly dominant-negative, effect.

The embryos developed heart size and morphology defects with cardiac edema, a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle, and reduced mitochondrial coverage along motoneuron axons. These findings were consistent with a dominant effect.

checks.claim: Flex et al. (2023) injected zebrafish embryos with mRNA encoding KIF5B T195K.
checks.evidence_quote: the c.584C > A missense substitution (p.Thr195Lys), the latter as representative of the pathogenic variants identified in individuals presenting with KIF5B-related KD, were transcribed in vitro and mRNAs were first injected into 1-cell stage zebrafish
checks.explanation: The text states T195K mRNA was injected into zebrafish embryos.

checks.claim: Zebrafish embryos injected with KIF5B T195K mRNA developed heart size and morphology defects with cardiac edema.
checks.evidence_quote: Overexpression of KIF5BThr195Lys and KIF5BAsn255del resulted in a wide range of morphological defects in heart size and anatomy, which were scored as mild or severe, and embryos expressing these variants presented heart oedemas at 2 dpf
checks.explanation: The text states heart size/anatomy defects with edema.

checks.claim: Zebrafish embryos injected with KIF5B T195K mRNA developed a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle.
checks.evidence_quote: the ceratohyal cartilage angle was less acute in all of the embryos injected with mutant KIF5B variants compared to those expressing the WT protein or non-injected embryos
checks.explanation: 'Less acute' means a wider angle, and this applies to all mutants.

checks.claim: Zebrafish embryos injected with KIF5B T195K mRNA had reduced mitochondrial coverage along motoneuron axons.
checks.evidence_quote: in particular for p.Thr195Lys and p.Leu498Pro alleles where we measured a significant reduction in the mitochondrial coverage along the axon
checks.explanation: The text states a significant reduction for T195K.

checks.claim: The zebrafish findings with KIF5B T195K were consistent with a dominant effect.
checks.evidence_quote: These results are in line with the observed phenotypes in the zebrafish null mutant, and support the hypothesis that these variants behave as dominant alleles in vivo.
checks.explanation: The text states the variants behave as dominant alleles.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) found a de novo heterozygous c.701G-T transversion in the KIF5B gene, resulting in a gly234-to-val (G234V) substitution, in 1 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. The mutation was identified by whole-exome sequencing. It affects a conserved residue in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain.

checks.claim: Itai et al. (2022) found a de novo heterozygous c.701G-T transversion in the KIF5B gene, resulting in a gly234-to-val (G234V) substitution, in 1 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: one with c.584C>A:p.(Thr195Lys), and the other with c.701G>T:p.(Gly234Val)
checks.explanation: Directly stated; de novo heterozygous applies to all.

checks.claim: The KIF5B G234V mutation was identified by whole-exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed whole-exome sequencing and evaluated the pathogenicity of the identified variants.
checks.explanation: Variants identified by WES.

checks.claim: The KIF5B G234V mutation affects a conserved residue.
checks.evidence_quote: All variants involved conserved amino acids
checks.explanation: Applies to G234V.

checks.claim: The KIF5B G234V mutation is in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain.
checks.evidence_quote: All variants involved conserved amino acids in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of the KIF5B protein.
checks.explanation: Applies to G234V.
